name: Le Morne Cultural Landscape
description: Le Morne is a 556-metre basalt mountain rising from a peninsula at the southwestern tip of Mauritius, ringed by a turquoise lagoon. Its steep, wooded cliffs, caves and broad summit sheltered escaped slaves, known as maroons, in the 18th and early 19th centuries. Oral traditions have made it a symbol of resistance and the island's "Maroon republic.
